The elasticity of the optimal search intensity \(q\) with respect to the unemployment probability \(p\) is computed from the government’s optimization problem. The worker’s optimal search intensity when unemployed is \(q = \frac{1}{2}\ln(20/b)\). The government chooses \(b\) (and thus \(q\)) to maximize expected utility subject to a balanced budget. The first‑order condition yields an implicit relation between \(q\) and \(p\). Differentiating this relation around \(p=0.2\) gives \(\frac{dq}{dp} \approx 0.1216\) and \(q \approx 0.9284\). Hence the elasticity is \(\frac{dq}{dp}\cdot\frac{p}{q} \approx 0.0262\), which rounds to \(0.026\).
